facts.text: Iowa Colony was founded in 1908 by the Emigration Land Company of Des Moines, Iowa, and its name honors the settlers who came from that state.
Rice farming began in Iowa Colony in 1920, marking the town’s early agricultural shift from its original ranching roots.
The 1948 discovery of oil brought a boom of regional employment and helped shape Iowa Colony’s mid‑century growth.
In the early 1990s, Iowa Colony gained notoriety as a major speed trap, inspiring a Texas law that limits municipal profits from such practices.
Iowa Colony sits in northern Brazoria County, just 22 miles south of downtown Houston, making it part of the larger Houston metropolitan area.
The town’s post office opened in 1919, closed by 1961, yet the community continued to grow during the 1960s as part of the expanding Houston region.
